sources.caveat: Categorical 30 m product. Land cover is point-sampled at the 0.05-degree cell center, so a cell represents the class at its center, not a fraction of its area; cell means across a zone are the proportion of sampled centers in each class. The derived cover signals use the same class mapping as the legacy NLCD sampler so eastern and western semantics stay identical.
sources.citation: U.S. Geological Survey, 2025, Annual NLCD (National Land Cover Database) Collection 1 Version 2 land cover, 2023.
sources.crs: CONUS Albers Equal Area (EPSG:5070 parameters; file proj string 'AEA WGS84')
sources.dataset: Annual NLCD Land Cover, CONUS, 2023, Collection 1 Version 2

sources.caveat: Percent canopy cover pixel values 0-100; 254 is the non-processing area and 255 the background, both stored as NULL. The canopy product is 2021 while the pinned land-cover product is 2023; the two-year difference is documented rather than corrected. Canopy is forest-structure evidence, never a host substitute: a spruce-specific mapped forest type stays more informative than generic canopy.
sources.citation: USDA Forest Service, 2023. NLCD Tree Canopy Cover (CONUS) v2021-4. Housman, I.; Heyer, J.; et al., methods documented in the distributed product metadata.
sources.crs: CONUS Albers Equal Area (EPSG:5070 parameters; file proj string 'Albers Conical Equal Area')
sources.dataset: NLCD Tree Canopy Cover (CONUS), v2021-4

sources.caveat: SSURGO coverage only. One query per state supplies the authoritative mapunit aggregate attributes; one batched point-in-mapunit query per tile resolves the sampled grid cells. A sampled point with no mapunit, and any attribute the mapunit does not publish, stays NULL. STATSGO2 gap filling is deliberately NOT applied here because it would present coarse state-level data as survey-grade soil.
sources.dataset: SSURGO (Soil Survey Geographic Database) via Soil Data Access

source.caveat: The hosted service does not state its PAD-US edition; it was not freshly audited in this pass. ST_Name supplies the authoritative state jurisdiction used for collecting-rule scoping.

PAD-US ST_Name is 'Not Applicable' for federal units, so it cannot supply jurisdiction. Jurisdiction is assigned here by point-in-polygon against the Census state boundaries and the raw PAD-US label is retained separately for audit.
source.citation: U.S. Census Bureau. 2023. Cartographic Boundary Files, state boundaries (1:20,000,000).

publicLands.statusNote: PAD-US public-access polygons intersecting this tile, clipped to the tile and each assigned an authoritative state jurisdiction by point-in-polygon. PAD-US ST_Name is discarded as jurisdiction because it reads 'Not Applicable' for federal units. Same-named units are grouped, so two different parks sharing a name inside one tile are merged. Rows without a resolved state are dropped: an unknown jurisdiction must not inherit any state-scoped rule.

accessPoints.statusNote: Normalized source and provenance sidecar required.

source.caveat: MTBS maps large fires only. The absence of a perimeter does not mean no fire; missing burn evidence must never be scored as a negative biological signal. The polygon layer carries dNBR offset/thresholds per fire but no single per-fire severity class, so severity is written NULL.
source.citation: MTBS maps the location, extent and severity of large fires (>= 1000 acres in the western U.S.) from the Landsat archive, 1984 onward.
source.provider: USDA Forest Service / USGS Monitoring Trends in Burn Severity

fireHistory.statusNote: MTBS burned-area boundaries intersecting this tile. Large fires only; the absence of a perimeter is not evidence that no fire occurred. Severity is not published per perimeter.

sources.releaseResolution: Each tile resolves its latest release from the public TNM bucket listing; cached tiles keep the release they were fetched with. Release dates in this release vary by tile (2022-2026) and are recorded per tile in the habitat sidecar source entries.

sources.dataset: SSURGO (Soil Survey Geographic Database) via Soil Data Access
sources.note: One state attribute query plus one batched point-to-MUKEY query per tile; no per-point Soil Data Access calls. Missing mapunit or attribute stays NULL. gSSURGO/gNATSGO state packages are supported through the same normalized contract when an operator supplies one.

sources.dataset: OSM access features (parking, trailheads, boat ramps, public gates, visitor areas)

summary.coverage: Bounded Southern Rockies release: 11 one-degree Colorado tiles (n37_w106..n39_w108 plus the two verified Front Range / Never Summer tiles n40_w106 and n40_w107), each with habitat, public-land and fire layers. Every release tile carries real FIA forest type groups, 3DEP elevation, Annual NLCD 2023 land cover, NLCD TCC 2021 canopy and real NRCS SSURGO soil (Soil Data Access). Access points remain UNBUILT and the manifest says so. This is not CONUS coverage; the 40 legacy Ohio/Tennessee tiles remain as previously published.
summary.layerStatusSemantics: populated = AVAILABLE or PARTIAL with a real asset; verifiedEmpty = complete source query with zero rows; unbuilt = no normalized source or missing required component; failed = build error. Counts are publication declarations, not a live HTTP audit. habitat.components is the authoritative per-component completeness map.

biology.note: EPA assignment is national; forecasting models are not. Collecting-rule scope requires a known state jurisdiction.

landCover.land_class: Annual NLCD class name sampled at the cell center
landCover.forest: 1 when the NLCD class is deciduous/evergreen/mixed/woody wetland

habitatSchema.canopy: 0..1 tree canopy fraction from NLCD TCC percent; NULL outside coverage

forestType.forest_mapped: 1 when a forest type group is mapped (class 0 means none mapped, not missing)
forestType.signals: oak_hickory, beech_maple, elm_ash_cottonwood (eastern) and spruce_fir, fir_spruce_mountain_hemlock, lodgepole_pine, ponderosa_pine, douglas_fir, aspen_birch (western); a signal is 1.0 exactly when the mapped class matches

soil.source: SSURGO via Soil Data Access by default; gSSURGO/gNATSGO packages are drop-in alternates
soil.missingSemantics: A sampled point with no mapunit, and any attribute a mapunit does not publish, stays NULL; no neutral value is invented.

terrain.elevation_ft: feet; the 3DEP source is meters and is converted once

habitatSchema.disturbance: never a habitat column: MTBS perimeters are a separate per-tile fire layer
habitatSchema.missingSemantics: Missing evidence is NULL, never 0. Legacy eastern tiles predate the additive land-cover fields and read them as NULL. Eastern host keys are never repurposed for western classes.
habitatSchema.componentSemantics: habitat.components declares forestType/elevation/landCover/canopy/soil as AVAILABLE or UNBUILT; habitat.status is AVAILABLE only when every required component (forestType, elevation, landCover, canopy) is present, otherwise PARTIAL. Soil additionally reports AVAILABLE when real NRCS soil evidence was composed. A Parquet file existing is not completeness.
